{{Short description|Construct in theoretical physics}}

In theoretical physics, [[Eugene Wigner]] and [[Erdal İnönü]] have discussed<ref>{{harvnb|Inönü|Wigner|1953}}</ref> the possibility to obtain from a given [[Lie group]] a different (non-isomorphic) Lie group by a '''group contraction''' with respect to a continuous subgroup of it. That amounts to a limiting operation on a parameter of the [[Lie algebra]], altering the [[structure constant]]s of this Lie algebra in a nontrivial singular<!--<ref>''Singular'' means that one performs a linear transformation on the Lie algebra where the corresponding change of basis matrix is singular. Equivalently, one may think of it as a change of basis where the new basis don't actually span the whole Lie [[algebra]]. Thereby one obtains new structure constants. The image under this transformation is then the new Lie algebra. The matrix is obtained as a limiting case of non-singular matrices, see {{harvtxt|Inönü|Wigner|1953|p=511}}</ref>--> manner, under suitable circumstances.<ref>{{harvnb|Segal|1951|p=221}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Saletan|1961|p=1}}</ref>

For example, [[Cross product|the Lie algebra]] of the [[3D rotation group]] {{math|SO(3)}}, {{math|1=[''X''<sub>1</sub>, ''X''<sub>2</sub>] = ''X''<sub>3</sub>}}, etc., may be rewritten by a change of variables {{math|1=''Y''<sub>1</sub> = ''εX''<sub>1</sub>}}, {{math|1=''Y''<sub>2</sub> = ''εX''<sub>2</sub>}}, {{math|1=''Y''<sub>3</sub> = ''X''<sub>3</sub>}}, as

: {{math|1=[''Y''<sub>1</sub>, ''Y''<sub>2</sub>] = ''ε''<sup>2</sup> ''Y''<sub>3</sub>, &nbsp; &nbsp; [''Y''<sub>2</sub>, ''Y''<sub>3</sub>] = ''Y''<sub>1</sub>, &nbsp; &nbsp; [''Y''<sub>3</sub>, ''Y''<sub>1</sub>] = ''Y''<sub>2</sub>}}.

The contraction limit {{math|''ε'' → 0}} trivializes the first commutator and thus yields the non-isomorphic algebra of the plane [[Euclidean group]], {{math|E<sub>2</sub> ~ ISO(2)}}. (This is isomorphic to the cylindrical group, describing motions of a point on the surface of a cylinder. It is the [[little group]], or [[stabilizer subgroup]], of null [[four-vectors]] in [[Minkowski space]].)  Specifically, the translation generators {{math|''Y''<sub>1</sub>, ''Y''<sub>2</sub>}}, now generate the Abelian [[normal subgroup]] of {{math|E<sub>2</sub>}}  (cf. [[Group extension]]), the [[Lorentz group#Parabolic|parabolic Lorentz transformations]].

Similar limits, of considerable application in physics (cf. [[correspondence principle]]s),  contract
* the [[de Sitter space|de Sitter group]] {{math|SO(4, 1) ~ Sp(2, 2)}} to the [[Poincaré group]] {{math|ISO(3, 1)}}, as the de Sitter radius diverges: {{math|''R'' → ∞}}; or
* the super-[[anti-de Sitter space|anti-de Sitter]] algebra to the [[super-Poincaré algebra]] as the AdS radius diverges {{math|''R'' → ∞}}; or
* the [[Poincaré group]] to the [[Galilean transformation#Galilean group|Galilei group]], as the [[speed of light]] diverges: {{nowrap|''c'' → ∞}};<ref>{{harvnb|Gilmore|2006}}</ref> or
* the [[Moyal bracket]] Lie algebra (equivalent to quantum commutators) to the [[Poisson bracket]] Lie algebra, in the [[classical limit]] as the [[Planck constant]] vanishes: {{nowrap|''ħ'' → 0}}.
